title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
value.en: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.
value.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.

value.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。
value.en: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.
value.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.

value.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
value.en: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.

value.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
value.en: The court recruited eminent tutors—He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
value.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

value.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。
value.en: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.
value.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.

value.zh: 其遊處左右，宜得正人使共周旋，能相長益者。」
value.en: Those about him in leisure and attendance should be upright men who keep company with him and help one another improve."
value.literal: Those who attend him in leisure and service should be upright men who may keep company with him and mutually aid one another's growth."

value.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。
value.en: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.
value.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.

value.zh: 資治通鑑 第136卷
value.en: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 136
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror for Government, Volume 136

value.zh: 世祖武皇帝上之下永明二年（
value.en: Emperor Wu of Qi (first section, lower part), Yongming year 2 (
value.literal: Emperor Wu the Founder, upper section part 2, Yongming year 2 (

value.zh: 甲子，公元四八四年）
value.en: jiazi, corresponding to 484 CE)
value.literal: jiazi, the year 484 CE)

value.zh: 春，正月，乙亥，以後將軍柳世隆為尚書右僕射；
value.en: In spring, the first month, on yihai, Rear General Liu Shilong was appointed Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing;
value.literal: In spring, the first month, on yihai, Rear General Liu Shilong was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing;

value.zh: 竟陵王子良為護軍將軍兼司徒，領兵置佐，鎮西州。
value.en: Prince Jingling Xiao Ziliang was made Protector-General of the Army and concurrently Minister over the Masses; he took on military aides and garrisoned West Province.
value.literal: Prince Jingling of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, was made Protector-General of the Army and concurrently Minister over the Masses, with military staff appointed, garrisoning West Province.

value.zh: 子良少有清尚，傾意賓客，才俊之士，皆游集其門。
value.en: From youth Ziliang had refined tastes and lavished attention on his guests; talented men of every sort flocked to his house.
value.literal: Ziliang from youth had pure and lofty tastes, devoted himself to guests, and men of talent all gathered at his gate.

value.zh: 開西邸，多聚古人器服以充之。
value.en: He opened the Western Lodge and filled it with antiquities—vessels and vestments from former ages.
value.literal: He opened the Western Lodge and gathered many ancient vessels and vestments to fill it.

value.zh: 記室參軍范雲、蕭琛、樂安任昉、法曹參軍王融、衛軍東閣祭酒蕭衍、鎮西功曹謝朓、步兵校尉沈約、揚州秀才吳郡陸倕，並以文學，尤見親待，號曰八友。
value.en: Recorder-General Fan Yun, Xiao Chen, Ren Fang of Le'an, Legal Affairs Officer Wang Rong, Eastern Pavilion Libationer Xiao Yan, West Garrison merit officer Xie Tiao, Footsoldier Commandant Shen Yue, and presented scholar Lu Chun of Wu—all celebrated for literature and especially cherished—were known as the Eight Friends.
value.literal: Recorder-General Fan Yun, Xiao Chen, Le'an Ren Fang, Legal Affairs Officer Wang Rong, Eastern Pavilion Libationer of the Guards Army Xiao Yan, Merit Officer of the West Garrison Xie Tiao, Footsoldier Commandant Shen Yue, and Yangzhou Presented Scholar Lu Chun of Wu Commandery—all famed for letters and especially favored—were called the Eight Friends.

value.zh: 法曹參軍柳惲、太學博士王僧孺、南徐州秀才濟陽江革、尚書殿中郎范縝、會稽孔休源亦預焉。
value.en: Liu Yun, Wang Sengru, Jiang Ge of Jiyang, Fan Zhen, and Kong Xiuyuan of Kuaiji were among them as well.
value.literal: Legal Affairs Officer Liu Yun, Erudite of the Imperial Academy Wang Sengru, South Xuzhou Presented Scholar Jiang Ge of Jiyang, Palace Attendant of the Masters of Writing Fan Zhen, and Kong Xiuyuan of Kuaiji also took part.

value.zh: 琛，惠開之從子；
value.en: Chen was a nephew of Hui Kai;
value.literal: Chen was the son of a younger brother of Hui Kai;

value.zh: 惲，元景之從孫；
value.en: Yun was a grandnephew of Yuanjing;
value.literal: Yun was a grandnephew of Yuanjing;

value.zh: 融，僧達之孫；
value.en: Rong was a grandson of Sengda;
value.literal: Rong was a grandson of Sengda;

value.zh: 衍，順之之子；
value.en: Yan was a son of Shunzhi;
value.literal: Yan was a son of Shunzhi;

value.zh: 朓，述之孫；
value.en: Tiao was a grandson of Shu;
value.literal: Tiao was a grandson of Shu;

value.zh: 約，璞之子；
value.en: Yue was a son of Pu;
value.literal: Yue was a son of Pu;

value.zh: 僧孺，雅之曾孫；
value.en: Sengru was a great-grandson of Yazhi;
value.literal: Sengru was a great-grandson of Yazhi;

value.zh: 縝，雲之從兄也。
value.en: Zhen was Yun's elder cousin.
value.literal: Zhen was Yun's elder cousin.

value.zh: 范縝盛稱無佛。
value.en: Fan Zhen loudly maintained that there is no Buddha.
value.literal: Fan Zhen loudly proclaimed that there is no Buddha.

value.zh: 子良曰：「君不信因果，何得有富貴、貧賤？」
value.en: Ziliang said, "If you do not believe in karma, how can there be rich and poor?"
value.literal: Ziliang said, "If you do not believe in cause and effect, how can there be wealth and honor, poverty and low estate?"

value.zh: 縝曰：「人生如樹花同發，隨風而散：或拂簾幌墜茵席之上，或關籬牆落糞溷之中。
value.en: Zhen replied, "Human life is like flowers on a tree blooming at once and scattering in the wind—some brush the curtain and land on cushions, others hit the fence and fall into the dung pit.
value.literal: Zhen said, "Human life is like blossoms on a tree blooming together and scattering with the wind: some brush the curtain and fall on cushions and mats, some strike the fence and fall into the privy.

value.zh: 墜茵席者，殿下是也；
value.en: Those who land on cushions—that is you, my lord;
value.literal: Those who fall on cushions and mats—that is Your Highness;

value.zh: 落糞溷者，下官是也。
value.en: those who fall into the dung pit—that is this humble official.
value.literal: those who fall into the privy—that is this humble official.

value.zh: 貴賤雖復殊途，因果竟在何處！」
value.en: Noble and base may take different paths—where then is karma!"
value.literal: Noble and base may take different paths, but where after all is cause and effect!"

value.zh: 子良無以難。
value.en: Ziliang had no answer.
value.literal: Ziliang had nothing with which to refute him.

value.zh: 縝又著《神滅論》，以為：「形者神之質，神者形之用也。
value.en: Zhen also wrote "On the Destruction of the Soul," arguing that "the body is the substance of the spirit, and the spirit is the function of the body.
value.literal: Zhen also wrote "On the Destruction of the Soul," holding that "the body is the substance of the spirit; the spirit is the function of the body.

value.zh: 神之於形，猶利之於刀；
value.en: The spirit in relation to the body is like sharpness to a blade;
value.literal: The spirit in relation to the body is like sharpness in relation to a knife;

value.zh: 未聞刀沒而利存，豈容形亡而神在哉！」
value.en: no one has heard of the blade vanishing while sharpness remains—how then could the body perish while the spirit endures!"
value.literal: one has never heard of the knife perishing while sharpness remains—how could the body perish while the spirit endures!"

value.zh: 此論出，朝野喧嘩，難之，終不能屈。
value.en: When the treatise appeared, court and country were in an uproar; critics assailed it, but none could refute him in the end.
value.literal: When this treatise appeared, court and countryside clamored; many challenged it, but in the end none could overcome him.

value.zh: 太原王琰著論譏縝曰：「嗚呼范子！
value.en: Wang Yan of Taiyuan wrote a treatise mocking Zhen: "Alas, Master Fan!
value.literal: Wang Yan of Taiyuan wrote a treatise to mock Zhen, saying, "Alas, Master Fan!

value.zh: 曾不知其先祖神靈所在！」
value.en: You do not even know where the spirits of your ancestors abide!"
value.literal: You do not even know where the spirits of your ancestors abide!"

value.zh: 欲以杜縝後對。
value.en: He meant to silence any reply from Zhen.
value.literal: He wished thereby to block Zhen from replying.

value.zh: 縝對曰：「嗚呼王子！
value.en: Zhen replied, "Alas, Master Wang!
value.literal: Zhen replied, "Alas, Master Wang!

value.zh: 知其先祖神靈所在，而不能殺身以從之！」
value.en: You know where your ancestors' spirits abide, yet you cannot kill yourself to join them!"
value.literal: You know where the spirits of your ancestors abide, yet cannot kill yourself to follow them!"

value.zh: 子良使王融謂之曰：「以卿才美，何患不至中書郎；
value.en: Ziliang sent Wang Rong to tell him, "With your talent, why should you fail to reach Director of the Palace Secretariat;
value.literal: Ziliang sent Wang Rong to tell him, "With your talent and beauty, why worry that you will not reach Director of the Palace Secretariat;

value.zh: 而故乖剌為此論，甚可惜也！
value.en: yet you deliberately go against the grain with this thesis—how regrettable!
value.literal: yet you deliberately go against the grain with this thesis—how very regrettable!

value.zh: 宜急毀棄之。」
value.en: You should destroy it at once."
value.literal: You should hurry to destroy and abandon it."

value.zh: 縝大笑曰：「使范縝賣論取官，已至令、僕矣，何但中書郎邪！」
value.en: Zhen laughed and said, "If Fan Zhen sold his thesis for office, he would already be Minister or Vice Minister—why settle for mere Director of the Palace Secretariat!"
value.literal: Zhen laughed loudly and said, "If Fan Zhen were to sell his thesis for office, he would already have reached Minister and Vice Minister—why only Director of the Palace Secretariat!"

value.zh: 資治通鑑 第139卷
value.en: Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Governance, Volume 139
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Governance, Volume 139

value.zh: 二月，乙丑，魏主如河陰，規方澤。
value.en: In the second month, on the yichou day, the Wei emperor went to Heyin to plan the square altar to Earth.
value.literal: In the second month, on day yichou, the Wei sovereign went to Heyin to plan the square altar to Earth.

value.zh: 臣光曰：孔子稱「鄙夫不可與事君，未得之，患得之；
value.en: Sima Guang comments: Confucius said, "A vulgar man is unfit to serve his sovereign; before he gains office, he fears he will not gain it;
value.literal: Minister Guang says: Confucius said, "The base fellow cannot be entrusted with serving a ruler; before obtaining it, he worries he will not obtain it;

value.zh: 既得之，患失之。
value.en: Once he holds it, he fears he will lose it.
value.literal: Once he has obtained it, he worries he will lose it.

value.zh: 苟患失之，無所不至。」
value.en: If he dreads losing what he has, there is no limit to what he will do."
value.literal: If he worries about losing it, there is nothing to which he will not go."

value.zh: 王融乘危徼幸，謀易嗣君。
value.en: Wang Rong seized a moment of crisis to gamble for advantage and schemed to replace the heir apparent.
value.literal: Wang Rong, riding peril to seek fortune, plotted to change the heir.

value.zh: 子良當時賢王，雖素以忠慎自居，不免憂死。
value.en: Ziliang was the most admired prince of his day; though he had always prided himself on loyalty and prudence, he still died of anxiety.
value.literal: Ziliang was the worthy prince of the time; though he had always taken loyalty and caution as his stand, he could not escape dying of worry.

value.zh: 跡其所以然，正由融速求富貴而已。
value.en: Trace the cause to its root, and it was nothing more than Rong's rush to seize wealth and status.
value.literal: Tracing why this came about, it was simply because Rong was hastening to seek wealth and rank.

value.zh: 輕躁之士，烏可近哉！
value.en: How can anyone keep company with a man so rash and unstable!
value.literal: A frivolous and impetuous fellow— how can one draw near to him!
